case.question: How do I reboot the module if it freezes?
case.expected_behavior: Pull the reset pin (pin 17) low for 100-500 ms, or use a restart command.

result.question: How do I reboot the module if it freezes?
result.answer: If the module software does not respond, you can reset it by pulling Pin 17 (RSTN) low for 100-500ms [HW-v5.3-p031-2]. Alternatively, the module supports an AT command reset using the command AT+TRB to restart the module [HW-v5.3-p031-2]. On the EVK, there is also an orange RESET button available [EVK-v1.1-p017-1].

case.question: How do I switch the EVK between USB power and a wall adapter?

result.question: How do I switch the EVK between USB power and a wall adapter?
result.answer: To switch the EVK between USB power and a wall adapter, use Jumper 3 (JMP 3) [EVK-v1.1-p012-1]. Placing the jumper in the first position enables USB Type-C as the input voltage source, while the second position enables the +5V Adapter as the voltage source [EVK-v1.1-p012-1]. You must place the Power Input Jumper (JMP 3) according to the input power supply being used [EVK-v1.1-p016-1].

case.question: Can the module find its location with satellites?
case.expected_behavior: Optional GNSS with GPS and BeiDou (GNSS variants).

result.question: Can the module find its location with satellites?
result.answer: Yes, the C16QS module includes optional integrated GNSS support for GPS and BeiDou constellations to provide location tracking [WEB-snapshot-20261114-c81b8bc8-s09, WEB-snapshot-20261114-c81b8bc8-s20, WEB-snapshot-20261114-c81b8bc8-s03]. The module supports AT commands for GNSS data, such as AT+CGPSGPOS for retrieving time, position, and fix data [AT-v3.1-p151-1]. For successful execution of GNSS commands, the GNSS_RXD pin (pin 83) must be left floating [AT-v3.1-p154-1].

case.question: How can I tell that the module has joined the mobile network?
case.expected_behavior: Network status indication pin/LED (NET_STATUS); on the EVK the NETLIGHT LED.

result.question: How can I tell that the module has joined the mobile network?
result.answer: You can determine if the module has joined the mobile network using the NET_STATUS pin (pin 21 or 75). When the module is latched on to a 4G or non-4G network for voice, SMS, and other services, the network indicator LED will be constantly bright [HW-v5.3-p040-1]. Alternatively, you can use the AT+CEREG command to enable network registration unsolicited result codes, which provide the registration status <stat> [AT-v3.1-p039-1]. Once RF functionality is enabled via AT+CFUN=1, the NETLIGHT will be stable when latched on to the network [EVK-v1.1-p018-1].
